name: Financial year — as the Companies Act, 2013 defines it (s.2(41))
definition: The financial year of a company or body corporate is the period ending on the 31st day of March every year; and where it has been incorporated on or after the 1st day of January of a year, the period ending on the 31st day of March of the following year — that is, the period in respect of which the financial statement is made up.
why_it_exists: Every other obligation is measured in financial years: books are kept for every financial year (s.128(1)), retained for eight of them (s.128(5)), and a financial statement is made up for one (s.2(40)). If the period is not fixed, none of those is countable. The 1 January rule stops a newly incorporated company from having to close a stub period of under three months.
inputs: the date of incorporation of the company or body corporate
outputs: the start and end dates of the financial year in respect of which the financial statement is made up
preconditions: the entity is a company or body corporate to which the Companies Act, 2013 applies
rules: UNKNOWN — no separate rule file is derived from s.2(41); it is a definition consumed by CO-BOOKS-RETENTION-001 and CO-FS-TRUE-AND-FAIR-001
exceptions: first proviso to s.2(41) — a holding, subsidiary or associate company of a company incorporated outside India that is required to follow a different financial year for consolidation of its accounts abroad may be allowed any period as its financial year by the Central Government, whether or not that period is a year
third proviso to s.2(41) — a company or body corporate existing at the commencement of the Act had two years from that commencement to align its financial year to this clause
UNKNOWN — source is the Act as enacted 2013; amendments not held locally
common_mistakes: using a calendar year, or a foreign parent's year end, without the Central Government allowance under the first proviso
closing a stub period for a company incorporated on or after 1 January — its first financial year runs to 31 March of the FOLLOWING year
assuming the Tribunal decides these applications — the printed first proviso is substituted text and names the Central Government, leaving the Tribunal only pending applications
icai_references: NOT APPLICABLE — the financial year is fixed by statute, not by an accounting standard
gst_references: NOT APPLICABLE — the GST tax period is a separate determination under the CGST Act and must not be conflated with s.2(41)
evidence_required: the date of incorporation, to decide whether the 1 January rule applies
where a non-standard year is claimed: the Central Government allowance under the first proviso
confidence_factors: weak when the date of incorporation is unknown — it decides the length of the first financial year
weak for a subsidiary or associate of a foreign parent — a Central Government allowance may displace the 31 March end
the whole first proviso carries a footnote recording substitution by Act 22 of 2019, so it is not the 2013 text
validation_checks: the period ends on 31 March, unless a Central Government allowance under the first proviso is on record
for a company incorporated on or after 1 January, the first financial year ends on 31 March of the following year
the financial statement is made up in respect of exactly this period
examples: a company incorporated on 15 February 2020 — its first financial year ends 31 March 2021, because it was incorporated on or after the 1st day of January of that year
counterexamples: a subsidiary of a foreign parent adopting a 31 December year end on its own initiative — the first proviso requires the Central Government to allow it
